title: Impact of Hospital Choice on 30-Day Mortality

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Two-Stage Least Squares (Instrumental Variables).  
• Treatment (endogenous): x = hospital chosen.  
• Instrument: z = ambulance diversion indicator (takes value 1 if usual hospital is on diversion).  

Why IV? Hospital choice is plausibly endogenous – sicker patients might be routed to (or self-select into) particular hospitals, biasing OLS. Ambulance diversion generates quasi-random variation in hospital assignment that is plausibly unrelated to individual unobservables affecting mortality, making it a valid instrument.

Key assumptions  
1. Relevance – Diversion meaningfully shifts hospital choice: Cov(z,x) ≠ 0 (first-stage F-stat > 10).  
2. Exclusion – Diversion affects 30-day mortality only through the hospital ultimately chosen, not through any other direct channel after controlling for observed patient characteristics.  
3. Independence/Random assignment – Conditional on controls, diversion is as-good-as random with respect to potential outcomes.  
4. Monotonicity – Diversion does not cause any patient who would otherwise go to Hospital B to switch to Hospital A (no “defiers”).  

## 2. R Code
```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
required <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
for(p in required){
  if(!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p, repos='http://cran.us.r-project.org')
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}

# ---- 1. Load data ----
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s82_data.csv")

# ---- 2. OLS benchmark ----
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)

# ---- 3. 2SLS / IV estimation ----
iv_mod <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)

# Robust (HC1) standard errors
robust_iv <- coeftest(iv_mod, vcov = vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC1"))

# ---- 4. First-stage strength ----
first_stage <- summary(lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df))
weakF <- first_stage$fstatistic[1]

# ---- 5. Reduced-form (effect of z on y) ----
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)

# ---- 6. Output key results ----
cat("-------------- Main Results --------------\n")
cat("OLS (biased):\n")
print(coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))["x",])

cat("\n2SLS (preferred):\n")
print(robust_iv["x",])

cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic on instrument z:", round(weakF,2), "\n")

cat("\nReduced-form effect of diversion (z) on mortality (y):\n")
print(coeftest(reduced_form, vcov = vcovHC(reduced_form, type = "HC1"))["z",])

cat("\n------------------------------------------\n")

# ---- 7. Simple robustness checks ----
# (i) Exclude controls
iv_nocontrol <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
cat("2SLS without controls, coef on x:\n")
print(coeftest(iv_nocontrol, vcov = vcovHC(iv_nocontrol, type = "HC1"))["x",])

# (ii) Add quadratic control term
df$controls_sq <- df$controls^2
iv_quad <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls_sq | z + controls + controls_sq, data = df)
cat("2SLS with quadratic controls, coef on x:\n")
print(coeftest(iv_quad, vcov = vcovHC(iv_quad, type = "HC1"))["x",])
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative. Being taken to a (presumably higher-quality or more appropriate) hospital because one’s preferred/closest facility is on diversion should reduce 30-day mortality, so the IV coefficient on hospital choice (x) is expected to be < 0.  

Magnitude: With the variables standardized (means ≈ 0, sd ≈ 1), a one-standard-deviation increase in the hospital-choice index might lower mortality by roughly 0.15–0.25 standard deviations (β̂ ≈ -0.15 to ‑0.25). The OLS estimate will likely be closer to zero (or even positive) because of adverse selection, whereas the 2SLS estimate should be larger in absolute value once endogeneity is addressed.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use ambulance diversion as an instrument for hospital choice.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Hospital choice significantly impacts 30-day mortality rates.
